chunks: And Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Aḥmad narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from al-‘Abbās ibn Ma’rūf, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from a man who said:

I asked about Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) regarding the saying of the Exalted: 'And whosoever is killed unjustly, then We have indeed given his heir an authority, but let him not exceed the limits in killing, verily he is helped.'

He (peace be upon him) said: This is about the Qā’im of the family of Muḥammad (peace be upon him and his family). He rises and kills avenging the blood of al-Ḥusain (peace be upon him). Even if he kills the people of the earth, he will not have exceeded the limits.
And His saying: 'but let him not exceed the limits in killing' means that he will not do anything that constitutes excess.
Then Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: I swear to Allāh that he will kill the descendants of the killers of al-Ḥusain (peace be upon him) for the deeds of their fathers.

key_terms.بِفَعَالِ آبَائِهَا: For the deeds of their fathers
key_terms.قَائِمُ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: The Qā’im of the family of Muḥammad (the Awaited Imam)

ai.seo_question: Who is the Qā’im referred to in the verse 'And whosoever is killed unjustly' and what is the meaning of his right to kill without excess?
ai.summary: This narration from Kamil al-Ziyarat interprets the 'authority' (sulṭān) in Quran 17:33 as the Qā’im, emphasizing that his vengeance for Ḥusain’s blood is divinely sanctioned to such an extent that killing all of humanity would not constitute excess (isrāf). It further specifies that he will execute the descendants of Ḥusain’s killers, applying the principle of holding children accountable for their fathers' deeds. This highlights the unique eschatological role of the Awaited Imam in avenging the Ahl al-Bayt.
